record.paper_title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
record.original_question: For an achievable Cantorval E, is a representing sequence (x_n) minimal exactly when the inequality x_n < r_{n+1} fails only finitely often, just as in the known characterization for achievable multi-interval sets?

evidence.quote: A sequence (xn) is a minimal representation of a Cantorval or a multi-interval set if removing any infinite subsequence changes the topological type of the achievement set.

It is known that if E is an achievable multi-interval set, then (xn) is a minimal representation for E if and only if xn < rn+1 for only finitely many n. Does this characterization remain valid when E is a Cantorval?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(x_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of positive real numbers with $\sum_{n=1}^\infty x_n < \infty$. The achievement set (set of subsums) of $(x_n)$ is
$$E(x_n) = \Big\{ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \varepsilon_n x_n : (\varepsilon_n) \in \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}} \Big\}.$$
For each $n$ let $r_n = \sum_{k=n}^{\infty} x_k$ denote the tail of the series. A nonempty compact subset of $\mathbb{R}$ is called:
- a multi-interval set if it is a finite union of nondegenerate closed intervals;
- a Cantorval if it is homeomorphic to the union of a Cantor set and countably many disjoint open intervals such that the endpoints of every component are accumulated by other components from both sides (equivalently, $E$ has uncountably many components but each component of the complement of $E$ in its convex hull has endpoints that are accumulated by other components).

Call $(x_n)$ a representation of $E$ if $E(x_n) = E$. Say that $(x_n)$ is a minimal representation of $E$ if removing any infinite subsequence from $(x_n)$ changes the topological type of $E(x_n)$ (i.e. the resulting achievement set is no longer a Cantorval, respectively no longer a multi-interval set, of the same type as $E$).

It is known that when $E$ is an achievable multi-interval set, $(x_n)$ is a minimal representation of $E$ if and only if the inequality $x_n < r_{n+1}$ fails for only finitely many $n$ (i.e. $x_n \ge r_{n+1}$ for only finitely many $n$, equivalently $x_n < r_{n+1}$ for all but finitely many $n$).

Question: Does the same characterization hold when $E$ is an achievable Cantorval? That is, prove or disprove: a representing sequence $(x_n)$ of a Cantorval $E$ is a minimal representation of $E$ if and only if $x_n < r_{n+1}$ holds for all but finitely many $n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in a recent (2025) survey of open problems on achievement sets, posed as an open problem about extending the known multi-interval characterization to Cantorvals. Related work (e.g. on locker sequences and uniqueness for Cantorvals) does not contain a full proof or disproof of this specific characterization, so the problem appears to still be open.

status_evidence.title: Set of Uniqueness for Cantorvals
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses minimal representations and locker conditions for Cantorvals but does not settle the stated equivalence.
